title: PDF attachments from Thunderbird fail DKIM at Microsoft; the same PDFs pass from Mailspring and webmail
creator: info2832
content:
Hello,

We would appreciate help narrowing down a reproducible delivery problem. PDF attachments sent from Thunderbird through our hosting provider are rejected by Microsoft. The same PDFs sent from Mailspring through the same SMTP server, using the same mailbox, are accepted with DKIM PASS. Webmail also works.

We are not assuming Thunderbird itself is at fault. A mail gateway might handle Thunderbird's message format differently. Our hosting provider, Vimexx, has been asked to investigate as well.

Setup - Windows 11; installed Thunderbird 161.0, release build 20261120171716. - Sender domain: ziektevrijleven.nl. Tests go to our own Microsoft/MSN mailbox. - SMTP: mail.zxcs.nl, port 465, SSL/TLS, normal password authentication. - Thunderbird's SMTP account/identity mapping and settings match the hosting provider's instructions. - DKIM is applied by the hosting service, not by Thunderbird. The signing domain is ziektevrijleven.nl, selector x.

Microsoft's rejection is 550 5.7.515, with SPF=PASS, DKIM=FAIL and DMARC=PASS.

Tests on 27 November 2026 (times are CET) 1. 09:08: Thunderbird with PDF A to a Hotmail address: rejected with that error. 2. 09:18: Roundcube webmail without an attachment to our own MSN mailbox: accepted. 3. 09:23: Thunderbird with PDF A to the same own MSN mailbox: rejected. 4. 09:25: Roundcube webmail with the same PDF A and visible message content: accepted. Webmail rebuilt the message; this was not a byte-identical resend. 5. 09:36: A new short Thunderbird message without an attachment: accepted. 6. 09:39: A short Thunderbird message with PDF A: rejected. 7. 09:41: A short Thunderbird message with a different PDF B: rejected. 8. 10:10: Mailspring without an attachment: accepted. 9. 10:13: Mailspring with PDF A: accepted. 10. 10:16: Mailspring with PDF B: accepted.

Microsoft's received Authentication-Results explicitly show SPF PASS, DKIM PASS, DMARC PASS and compauth PASS for every accepted test listed above. Both received Mailspring PDFs are byte-identical to the PDFs used in the failed Thunderbird tests, verified by SHA-256. The three Mailspring tests used the same subject and message text. The earlier Thunderbird tests used different short text/signatures, so this is not yet a strictly one-variable comparison between clients.

What we have checked - The currently published DKIM key matches the hosting control panel and several DNS resolvers. No DNS or DKIM settings were changed during these tests. - This is not confined to one outgoing relay: one hosting relay processed both accepted and rejected tests. - The failed messages contain ordinary plain text, HTML and PDF attachments, with no S/MIME or OpenPGP signing/encryption parts. - We have only inspected settings and extensions so far. Active extensions are Templates Reply 1.3, AutoZoom 1.4 and Thundermail 2.0.30; LanguageTool is disabled. - Troubleshoot Mode and a clean Thunderbird profile have NOT yet been tested. We have not reset the existing profile or altered MIME preferences.

Could you advise on the next diagnostic steps, preferably one change at a time? We would like to test Troubleshoot Mode first, then a temporary clean profile if necessary, and then any relevant message-format options. We would also welcome advice on what evidence would distinguish a Thunderbird issue from a downstream gateway changing the message after DKIM signing.

We found a possibly related Proxmox discussion, but do not know whether it applies to our provider's software/version: https://forum.proxmox.com/threads/pmg-breaks-dkim-on-outgoing-multipart-mails.125984/

Technical appendix - Both clients' attachment messages have multipart/mixed containing multipart/alternative (text/plain and text/html), followed by the PDF. Mailspring's success is therefore not evidence that HTML alone causes this. - In Thunderbird Sent copies, HTML uses 7bit, PDF MIME type is application/pdf, and base64 attachment lines normally contain 72 characters. - In the successful Mailspring messages received by Microsoft, HTML uses quoted-printable, PDF MIME type is application/octet-stream, and base64 attachment lines normally contain 76 characters. - Thunderbird's outer MIME preamble reads "This is a multi-part message in MIME format."; the received Mailspring copies have no preamble. These are observed differences, not established defects. The MIME parser reported no defects. - These comparisons use different stages: Thunderbird's Sent copy versus Mailspring's received copy. We cannot attribute every difference to the sending application alone. - The DKIM header signature in each failed delivery report verifies locally against the current public key. The body from its matching Sent copy matches the signed body hash, and the reconstructed message validates locally. However, the bounce includes the original headers but not the received body: we do NOT have the exact bytes Microsoft evaluated for the rejected messages. - PDF A: 1,141,473 bytes; SHA-256 45804f9239eb14bad9f40fd9b5692c4412beb42b1f90f729115cf2d826098192. - PDF B: 2,982,178 bytes; SHA-256 1124dc46ad5bfe231d22100cea414e539dbebb578f6b78c156fa788554998df5.

We can provide further sanitized technical details if useful. We have deliberately not included customer correspondence, personal recipient addresses, private PDFs, IP addresses, credentials or raw email files in this public report.

Thank you for helping us isolate the cause.

title: come consultare il mio calendario Thunderbird sul mio cellulare samsung
creator: amedeo.lauritano
content:
Buongiorno, utilizzo da moltissimi anni Thunderbird: per la mia agenda utilizzavo invece Yahoo Calendar Classic.

Purtroppo Yahoo ha deciso di cancellare la versione Classic: a questo punto ho migrato la mia agenda di più di 15 anni su TH Calendario e mi trovo bene.

Vorrei poter guardare l'agenda anche da cellulare (ho un Samsung): esiste un add-on che possa fare da bridge allo scopo?

Sono poco tecnologico: se ci fosse qualcosa di "automatico" sarebbe perfetto.

Sono disponibile a riconoscere un compenso a chi mi potesse aiutare.

Grazie e buona giornata. A
